US-526 CLOSED + COMMITTED as dd3a4cf (Sprint 70 / V0.29.25, 6/8 done -- only US-527/528/529 left). BL-029 stays CLEARED; commits work, no .git/index.lock.

*** TD-059 STALL, EIGHTH SIGHTING, AND THE WORST VARIANT YET. *** I booted into a tree where the ENTIRE US-526 implementation existed but was COMPLETELY UNCOMMITTED -- 5 untracked files (including both new src/ modules) plus 7 modified -- while sprint.json still said sprint-ready/passes:false, progress.txt had no entry, and this file still showed me active on it. US-525 was uncommitted too; US-524's was at least committed. Per the US-505 rule I re-ran the gate and VERIFIED instead of re-implementing. THE ORDERING IS THE FIX AND I WANT IT CARRIED: gate -> COMMIT -> then bookkeeping. The failure mode is never 'the code was wrong', it is always 'the close got dropped at the end', so getting the commit in early is what makes the iteration survivable. Proof it matters: an Iris commit (413cbc8) landed on the shared checkout BETWEEN my gate run and my commit.

VERIFY THE SEAMS, DO NOT TRUST AN INHERITED TREE. Four checks, any one of which failing would make the writer SILENTLY INERT while every unit test stayed green: PowerMonitor.onTransition exists (power.py:726); UpsMonitor.getVcell/getBatteryPercentage exist (ups_monitor.py:557/625); PowerSource.AC_POWER='ac_power'/BATTERY='battery' match the writer's value constants (types.py:107-108); and THE BIG ONE -- HardwareManager.upsMonitor is a PUBLIC property (hardware_manager.py:569) whose private store is _upsMonitor. Had it been private-only, getattr(hw,'upsMonitor') would return None forever and EVERY drain would record NULL vcell/soc while looking perfectly healthy. That is the honest-instrument-degrades-silently shape: not a crash, just permanent NULLs. Also confirmed TWO 'class PowerSource' definitions exist in src/pi/power (types.py + power_source_provider.py), which vindicates the .value-based comparison rather than merely excusing it.

TWO REAL FIXES THE GATE FOUND (the inherited tree was NOT green). (a) tests/scripts/test_record_drain_test.py::test_productionWriterUsesTheSameGuard was genuinely RED. It proves the SSOT claim -- one soc_calibration source file, two callers, no drifted copy -- via inspect.getsourcefile() STRING equality, but this shared checkout spells one file two ways: 'Z:\o\OBD2v2\...' (mapped drive) vs '\\chi-nas-01\PPS-Projects\O\OBD2v2\...' (its UNC target). So it reported 'different implementation' for an identical file -- a false alarm on the very invariant it guards. Fixed to os.path.samefile (asks the filesystem: st_dev/st_ino) and MUTATION-PROVED the teeth survived rather than just going green: a byte-identical copy at another path is still REJECTED (False), the alias is accepted (True). CARRY THIS: never assert path identity by string on this checkout. (b) ruff I001 on scripts/record_drain_test.py -- this repo's isort has combine-as-imports=false, so each 'as' alias needs its OWN import statement. I ran ruff --fix on that one touched file and it produced TWO NEW E402 errors, because the autofix split the statement WITHOUT carrying the '# noqa: E402' the file's sys.path bootstrap requires. Added back by hand. CARRY THIS TOO: 'fixed 1 error' is not 'clean' -- always re-run the check after a --fix on a file with noqa-bearing imports.

THE DESIGN DETAIL MOST WORTH KNOWING, because it is subtle and the shipped code gets it RIGHT: prePowerOffFn fires on BOTH poweroff paths, and the VCELL-FLOOR FAST PATH is the one that matters -- it SKIPS the pipeline, and that is precisely how a run-to-cutoff drain ends. A close implemented as a ShutdownTask would have missed every single row the depth-gate verdict needs. Second one: the reaper is narrowed to rows carrying DRAIN_OPEN_NOTE, STRICTER than Atlas's 'end_timestamp IS NULL' DoD, and that narrowing is load-bearing -- the four US-442 historical orphans (ids 1/9/18/21) hold end_timestamp NULL DELIBERATELY, so without the ownership marker the first power-restore close would feed a months-old row to endDrainEvent and mint a multi-month runtime WITH a real end_vcell_v, i.e. a row that looks QUALIFYING. Worse than the reaper trap the AC warned about.

AC7's depth-gate test is honest about US-527 not having landed: it asserts unknown/qualifyingCount==0 and documents that NULL runtime_seconds fails TODAY's runtime gate while NULL end_vcell_v fails Spool's FUTURE depth gate -- double-safe, so it holds across the US-527 remap instead of silently testing only the current gate.

GATE, SYNCHRONOUS, IN-LOOP, BEFORE THE COMMIT: 3 new test files = 50 passed with ZERO skips (skip count read on purpose per US-524); then the full scoped suites for the changed BASE modules (battery_health.py + controller.py + lifecycle.py are shared) -- tests/pi/power + tests/scripts = 205 passed, tests/pi/obdii/orchestrator = 24 passed, record_drain_test re-run after the import fix = 24 passed. ruff clean on all 11 touched .py files. PRE-EXISTING RED, NOT MINE, BOTH IN THIS SPRINT: TD-073 promise-tag lint = US-529; TD-075's 10 project-wide ruff errors mean `ruff check src/ tests/` exits 1 on a clean tree, so lint is per-touched-file. `make` is NOT on PATH -- `make lint` exits 127, which READS LIKE A PASS.

OWED, NOT FAKED: the live drill (real AC->battery->AC on the Pi + a battery_health_log query) needs a PM deploy (handbook 13), and the live unit is STILL the hand-patched pre-US-522 copy, so the deploy has not run since US-522. Tell whoever drills it: a NULL soc_pct is CORRECT if the transition happens inside the ~180 s MAX17048 cold-start window -- vcell will still be real, because only the modelled SoC needs the window. Do not file that as a bug.

NEXT UP: US-527 (verdict band-remap to Spool's depth gate) is the natural pair to what I just landed -- the writer now produces the rows it grades, and the AC is explicit that the [EXACT:3.50] V / [EXACT:60] s values and the good/degraded/replace bands must come from Spool's landed ruling 429a3ed, NOT from inference.
